subject: Urgent: Holloway on-prem performance incident — exec brief & mitigation
messages:
From: Danielle Reid <danielle.reid@hollowayai.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hollowayai.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: High p95 + spike in 5xx on our on-prem cluster (SFO)

Hi Irene / Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in inference p95 latency and a rise in 5xx errors on our SFO on-prem deployment starting ~02:30 PDT this morning. Affected routes are /chat and /summarize; user impact reported by our customer success team is about 18% of requests failing or timing out.

Attached a short KPI snapshot and the server trace for the primary node (svc_trace_20260815.log).

We need an urgent remediation plan and an exec-level summary for our CTO (Arjun) — they are requesting a 09:00 PT call tomorrow to discuss impact and next steps. Can Redwood provide immediate mitigations and a short SLA/credit proposal?

Thanks,
Danielle Reid
Head of Platform Engineering
Holloway AI

Attachments: holloway_kpi_snapshot.csv (CSV), svc_trace_20260815.log (log)
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: danielle.reid@hollowayai.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High p95 + spike in 5xx on our on-prem cluster (SFO)

Acknowledged — I saw the traces. Short plan: 1) immediate operational mitigations to lower error rate and roll back the client-impacting regression, 2) short-term config change to reduce tail latency, 3) schedule an exec brief & troubleshooting walkthrough for tomorrow 09:00 PT.

Immediate asks for the on-call ops team (Marissa / Markus / Evelyn):
- Run the KV-cache eviction diagnostic on node sfo-03, capture current resident set and eviction histogram.
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size to 8 for chat/summarize routes (hot path) and hold for 30m to measure p95 delta.
- Enable prefix caching bypass for requests < 256 tokens for the next 2 hours.

Marissa — can you confirm staff to run (1) and apply (2) now? I will prepare the exec brief and user-facing note. Naomi, please prepare an SLA credit draft for Holloway to review if we confirm a regression on our side.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, danielle.reid@hollowayai.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High p95 + spike in 5xx on our on-prem cluster (SFO) — initial root cause and quick mitigations

Quick technical summary from the triage on sfo-03:
- Observed sustained KV cache churn coincident with increased 5xx; memory RSS on the serving process is spiking and GC cycles are increasing.
- Recent deploy from Holloway (q4f quantized variant) shows higher transient working set; combined with longer context windows we are seeing frequent ephemeral allocations triggering cache eviction.
- Error pattern: backend OOM/Latency > 3s leading to thread timeouts (500s) under normal concurrency.

Recommended immediate actions (apply in this order):
1) Roll forward a config override: limit_concurrent_requests=120 -> 96 on sfo cluster; reduces head-of-line congestion.
2) Reduce max_batch_size to 6 for chat route via runtime config (hot reload).
3) Enable proactive KV pinning for known hot prefixes (we can push a list from Holloway GUIDs).

I applied a non-invasive probe (no restart) that lowers max_batch_size to 8 — current p95 for /chat dropped ~28% in the last 12m and 5xx rate halved. I will push to 6 if no regression in the next 15m.

Relevant trace excerpt (svc_trace_20260815.log attached) and the command I used:
- redwoodctl cluster update-config --cluster sfo --route chat --max-batch-size 8

Markus Klein
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@hollowayai.com>, Danielle Reid <danielle.reid@hollowayai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Planned exec brief + customer notification (draft) — Holloway on-prem impact

Arjun / Danielle —

TL;DR (for execs): We identified a regression correlated with a recent quantized model variant that increases transient memory pressure on your SFO on-prem serving nodes. Immediate mitigations reduced p95 and 5xx rates; we propose a short follow-up plan and compensation outline below.

What happened (2-3 lines):
- Starting 2026-08-15 02:30 PDT, routing on two servicing nodes experienced elevated KV eviction and GC pressure tied to the q4f variant and larger average context length.

Impact:~18% of requests to /chat and /summarize intermittently timed out or returned 500. Customer-facing incidents peaked for ~2.5 hours and then decreased after config changes.

What we did (immediate):
- Reduced runtime max_batch_size on hot routes (deployed non-disruptively) and applied a lower concurrency cap to reduce contention.
- Enabled temporary prefix bypass and proactive KV pinning.
- Ongoing: we are collecting a 24-hour trace and will run a controlled rollout of a quantization profile validated for on-prem memory patterns.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- Today 09:00 PT: 30m exec call to align on customer impact, remediation roadmap, and compensation (we propose a one-time credit and a technical post-mortem within 72 hours).
- 0–4 hours: Roll config hold (we continue monitoring).
- 24–72 hours: Controlled canary of an adjusted quant profile for Holloway with telemetry.

Attached: exec_brief_v1.pdf (one-page summary), proposed customer-facing note (draft in Drive: https://redwood.app/drive/holloway/exec-brief-v1).

Naomi — draft SLA credit proposal attached; please adjust if needed before the call.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec_brief_v1.pdf

Thanks — we appreciate the quick triage and the clear plan. 09:00 PT tomorrow works for Arjun and me. Two asks before the call:
1) Can you share the 15m rolling p95 and 5xx trend for the last 3 hours and the configuration change diffs (commands/history) so our SREs can cross-check?
2) Please provide the runbook steps you will execute if the adjusted quant profile causes renewed memory pressure during canary.

If you can drop those into the Drive link and share a short notification for customers that we can co-send, we'll be set for the call.

-Danielle

Holloway AI
